page: Microsoft Azure B2pls_v2 is a burstable, entry-tier virtual machine powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 2 arm64 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with a single thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU core. The virtual machine includes no local disk storage, relying instead on network-attached storage with Premium Storage capability, and does not provide included public IPv4 addresses or dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark measurements reflect the burstable resource profile and compact two-core arm64 footprint. In synthetic compute evaluations, the instance achieved an average stress-ng single-core score of 1821.89, while multi-core stress-ng reached 3614.38, placing it in the lower quartile. Geekbench scores registered at 1111.0 for single-core execution and 2010.0 for multi-core. Cryptographic throughput benefits from native hardware AES acceleration, though memory bandwidth tests yielded lower-tier throughput with 27.02 GB/sec uncached reads and 16.61 GB/sec uncached writes. Operational benchmarks showed 2.78 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.88 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

Engineered for budget-conscious and lightweight deployments, the B2pls_v2 delivers high qualitative cost efficiency when handling intermittent processing tasks. Because the burstable CPU model accumulates credits during idle periods to sustain occasional execution spikes, continuous heavy compute or data-intensive processing quickly exhausts burst capacity. With its modest 4.0 GB memory capacity and absence of local scratch storage, the server is suitable for lightweight microservices, intermittent staging environments, small-scale web serving, code repository mirrors, and development background tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure B2pls_v2 is an arm64 entry-tier virtual machine configured with 2 burstable vCPUs on an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz and 4.0 GB of system memory. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached volumes, and features no dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-threaded compute efficiency alongside modest multi-core and memory subsystem throughput, recording 1111.0 on Geekbench single-core and 27.02 GB/sec on uncached memory reads. Hardware AES acceleration supports cryptographic tasks, while application-level benchmarks indicate 2.78 million Redis SET operations per second. Given its burstable baseline and limited memory capacity, the B2pls_v2 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for variable, low-density workloads, including lightweight web serving, development sandboxes, and intermittent background utilities.
